changes.before: If Minutes changes from 15 to -2 while the JSON remains well formed, which branch runs?
changes.after: Read JSON text, then check that its data is allowed.

before: JSON is a text format for exchanging values. JsonSerializer.Serialize turns an object into JSON; Deserialize<T> attempts to build a T from JSON. The three-quote raw string literal below keeps JSON quote characters without backslash escapes.
Successful parsing does not prove your application rules. In this example, a valid goal needs a nonblank Title and nonnegative Minutes. A JSON null can also produce a null object.
The if condition rejects null, a blank title, or negative minutes. Only the else branch prints Accepted. JsonException catches malformed or incompatible JSON separately.
Goal has public properties with defaults. Those defaults are not proof that missing input was deliberately supplied; choose validation rules appropriate to the real application.
Expected behavior from this example: Accepted: {"Title":"Read","Minutes":15}. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer: Try null, a blank title, negative minutes and malformed JSON separately. Record which check rejects each one. This is a separate local practice task, not a requirement to mark the reading complete.
after: JSON is a text format for sharing data. Here it holds a title and a number of minutes. The three-quote C# string keeps the JSON's quote marks without extra escape characters.
Deserialize<Goal> tries to turn the JSON into a Goal object. Deserialize means rebuild a value from stored text. JSON containing null can produce a null result.
Reading the format successfully is only the first check. This program also requires an existing object, a title with more than spaces, and minutes of zero or more.
JsonException handles JSON that is broken or does not fit the expected types. The Rejected branch handles readable data that fails this program's rules.
The program prints Accepted: {"Title":"Read","Minutes":15}. Serialize turns the accepted object back into JSON text for this message.

A property may keep its default when input leaves it out. Here, a missing Title stays empty and is rejected, but missing Minutes stays zero and passes. A real app must decide whether missing and zero should mean different things.

before.question: If Minutes changes from 15 to -2 while the JSON remains well formed, which branch runs?
choices: Invalid JSON, because all negative numbers break JSON
Rejected, because the application validates Minutes
before.explanation: A negative JSON number parses as an int. The explicit Minutes < 0 rule rejects it afterward.

after.question: Keep valid JSON but change Minutes to -2. Which message is chosen?
after.explanation: A negative number is valid JSON. The program's separate Minutes < 0 rule rejects it.
